implementation_notes: LINQ makes a query a first-class language construct: the query expression (or its method syntax, Where/Select/SelectMany) is the ordered pipeline and each operator is a named stage over IEnumerable<T>, replacing the classic stage-list class. Evaluation is deferred - the chain runs only when a foreach, ToList or another terminal operation enumerates it - and the sequence composes lazily with no intermediate lists. Choose System.IO.Pipelines instead when the payload is bytes on a socket or stream rather than an object sequence.
pitfalls: Deferred execution means the query re-runs on every enumeration and captures variables by reference, so a pipeline enumerated twice does the work twice - possibly with changed inputs.
Each operator adds an enumerator layer; chaining over arrays or spans can be slower than a fused loop unless the data is large enough to amortise it.
Exceptions surface at the terminal operation, not where the stage was declared, which misattributes the failure unless stages are wrapped.

variants.name: System.IO.Pipelines byte pipeline
variants.idiom_name: PipeWriter / PipeReader with GetMemory, Advance and FlushAsync
variants.implementation_notes: System.IO.Pipelines is the .NET library for high-performance I/O pipelines: a Pipe hands out a PipeWriter and a PipeReader, the producer writes into GetMemory/GetSpan, calls Advance and FlushAsync, and the consumer reads with ReadAsync, consumes a ReadOnlySequence and reports progress with AdvanceTo (Microsoft docs). Backpressure is explicit - FlushAsync pauses and returns IsCompleted when the reader is done - so it replaces both the stage class and ad-hoc buffer management for socket or file byte streams. Keep LINQ for object pipelines, where the extra buffer protocol buys nothing.
pitfalls: PipeReader and PipeWriter are not thread-safe: exactly one owner per side, and concurrent access corrupts the buffer state.
ReadOnlySequence returned by ReadAsync is only valid until AdvanceTo; using it later reads recycled memory.
Forgetting to complete both sides leaks pooled buffers, and calling FlushAsync where the reader cannot start before the flush returns deadlocks the pipeline.
